answer: Graph-based kin detection with bonded edges: every agent posts a bond to join, and each payment or vouch it makes becomes an edge in a public graph. A sybil cluster grows like a lotus from one root, densely linked inward but tied to the honest network by a single thin jetty. When analysis flags that cut, every bond in the cluster is frozen and slashed at once, so a farmer risks all deposits together. Honest agents earn edges slowly across many unrelated peers, a ridge too costly for fakes to climb.
